Senses.Explanation: To guard the barrier is to occupy the checkpoint that an arriving person must pass. The direct exchange sends a questioner to ask the checkpoint official how to pass the barrier. Later speakers warn of meeting the checkpoint man ahead or say that guarding requires a barrier-guarding person. The phrase thereby names an encounter role, not simply shutting a physical gate.

Senses.Explanation: Gatekeeping is also the title of a collection or verse-cycle associated with Chan case material. A conduct record lists Gatekeeping among six works selected for circulation. Another chronology records ten Gatekeeping verses, while a question recalls a particular Gatekeeping saying. These are word, saying, and book titles, not a person physically guarding a checkpoint.
